data.description:
## Context / Problem

S1 [rebar:1934-63dd-4be9-4c48] lets a ticket assert `code_impact: none`, and S2 [rebar:749c-7546-6fe3-4d27] makes that
assertion buy real leverage: the attestation stops invalidating on code drift. An assertion
that buys leverage must be checkable, or "declare none" becomes the cheap way to silence the
drift gate. Nothing today reads the assertion for truthfulness.

The check belongs in plan review, where the plan text that would contradict the claim is
already in context. It must be a NARROW criterion: it fires ONLY on the presence of the
assertion, and on every other ticket it must not run at all (no cost, no false positives).

## Approach

Add one LLM criterion, id `no-code-impact`, whose entire job is: given a ticket that asserts it
requires no code changes, decide whether the plan the ticket actually describes requires code
changes.

**Trigger — presence of the assertion, deterministically.** `registry.applies`
(src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py:375) is the single proportionate-scrutiny seam, called
from exactly one place (orchestrator.py:374), which already holds `ctx.state`. It gains a
`code_impact` keyword and honours a new `applies_at.require_code_impact` list: a criterion
carrying `{"require_code_impact": ["none"]}` runs only when the ticket's state says `none`.
This is a deterministic gate, not an LLM-routed overlay — the assertion is a field, so its
presence is a fact, and only the CORRECTNESS judgment is left to the model. Every existing
criterion omits the key and is therefore unaffected.

**Judgment — the LLM's.** The rubric prompt
(`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_no_code_impact.md`, the naming convention
`plan_review_decomp_shape.md` uses for `decomp-shape`) gets the plan text and the declared
reason, and asks one question: does delivering THIS plan require changing code? It FAILS when
the plan describes work that cannot land without a source change — new/changed behavior, a new
flag or config key the code must read, a test to add, a generated artifact whose generator
lives in the tree — and PASSES when the deliverable genuinely lives outside the code
(prose-only documentation, a ticket/process action, an operator action in an external system,
a decision record). Anti-FP guidance keeps it off the two cases most likely to be
over-flagged: a docs change that merely DESCRIBES code is still docs; and a ticket whose only
artifact is a regenerated file whose generator it does not modify is still no-code, provided
the plan says so.

`exec: "1-TURN"`, `facet: "scope-intent"` (alongside `necessity`), `default_posture:
"advisory"`, `block_threshold: 0.95` — the repo's ship-advisory-then-dogfood-promote
convention (docs/plan-review-gate.md's promotion gate). It is registered in `CANONICAL_LLM`
so the completeness guard knows it, and the generated criteria guide is regenerated so
`rebar explain no-code-impact` works.

The completion verifier is criteria-free and is NOT touched by this story.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_no_code_impact.md` (new) — the rubric prompt with its
  front-matter contract, matching the shape of an existing 1-TURN criterion prompt.
- `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/index.json` — register the prompt.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json` — the routing entry, including
  `applies_at.require_code_impact: ["none"]` and the checklist.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` — `CANONICAL_LLM` membership; `applies()` gains the
  `code_impact` keyword and the `require_code_impact` condition; `_validate_routing_entry`
  accepts and type-checks the new key.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` — pass `code_impact=ctx.state.get("code_impact")`
  at the single `applies()` call site.
- `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` — regenerated via
  `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.registry regenerate-criteria-guide` (never hand-edited).

## Testing

- `applies()` table: a criterion with `require_code_impact: ["none"]` runs for a `none`
  ticket and is filtered out for `undeclared` and `paths`; a criterion WITHOUT the key is
  unaffected by any `code_impact` value (pins that no existing criterion's routing changes).
- Routing-parity gate (`registry.py`'s existing packaged-routing validator) passes with the
  new entry, and the criteria-guide regeneration is idempotent — running it twice leaves the
  file unchanged, and the committed file matches a fresh regeneration.
- Prompt-contract test in the style of the existing reviewer-prompt tests: the front matter
  parses and the criterion id resolves through `get_prompt`.
- Two rubric fixtures exercised through the offline judge path: a docs-only plan asserting
  `none` PASSES; a plan asserting `none` whose acceptance criteria require a new CLI flag
  FAILS with a finding naming the contradicting plan text.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ticket whose `code_impact` is `none` routes `no-code-impact` into the Pass-1 finder
      set; a ticket with `paths` or `undeclared` does not (checked: `applies()`/routing test
      asserting membership of the selected criteria list in all three states).
- [ ] The criterion returns a FAIL finding for a plan asserting `none` that requires a source
      change, and PASS for a genuinely prose-only plan (checked: the two rubric fixtures).
- [ ] `no-code-impact` is in `CANONICAL_LLM`, its routing entry passes the packaged-routing
      parity gate, and `rebar explain no-code-impact` prints its section (checked: parity gate
      + a CLI test).
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md` is a byte-exact product of the regeneration command
      (checked: the existing regeneration-idempotence test).
- [ ] Its posture is advisory: a FAIL from this criterion alone does not block a claim
      (checked: a gate test asserting the verdict stays claimable).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the full test suite pass.
data.title: Plan-review criterion no-code-impact: judge whether a no-code-changes assertion is correct
